PullRequest.Title: agentHost: keep workspaceless instructions stable across resume and forks
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #340431
Related: #342320 (separate issue: converting with `set_workspace` intentionally changes the prompt and misses the cache; not addressed here)

## Problem

A workspaceless chat's system prompt includes the `<workspaceless_chat>` block. Three Copilot launch paths decided the flag inconsistently:

| Path | Before |
|---|---|
| `_resumeSessionOnce` (default chat resumed by SDK id) | Read the flag from the SDK session's metadata, which normally doesn't store it, so it resolved to `false` and the block was dropped |
| `_resumeChatSessionOnce` (addressed chat backings) | Never forwarded the flag |
| `_mintChatBacking` fork and create plans (forks, side chats, other eagerly created chats) | Never set the flag |

Each disagreement changed the system prompt between launches of the same conversation, so the provider couldn't reuse the cached prompt. The resumed agent also lost its scratch-directory guidance.

## Fix

- `_readSessionMetadata` uses the host-owned `sessionSettings` for the owning session first. It falls back to the provider metadata only when the host has no settings. `??` keeps an explicit host `false` (for example after a workspace conversion) over a stale provider `"true"`.
- `_resumeChatSessionOnce` forwards the flag in its launch plan.
- `_mintChatBacking` sets the same host-owned flag on both its fork and create launch plans.

`launchPlan.workspaceless` only feeds the prompt registry, so nothing else changes.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A workspaceless chat was created with scratch guidance in its system prompt, but resume read the flag from the SDK-session database instead of the host-owned session state. When that provider metadata lacked the marker, resume dropped the guidance, changed the provider-bound system prompt, and invalidated exact-prefix prompt-cache reuse for the conversation's next model request.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: The first model turn after restoring a workspaceless conversation had to process an uncached changed system prompt, increasing prompt-prefill work and time to first output instead of reusing the conversation's warm prompt cache.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed lookup prefers the owning session's retained host setting and falls back to provider metadata only when the host has no value. The resume launch plan now receives the same workspaceless value as creation, keeping the system prompt stable so a resumed first turn can reuse the existing prompt cache rather than processing an altered prompt prefix.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this change, `_resumeSessionOnce` reads metadata for the SDK session URI and `_readSessionMetadata` derived `workspaceless` only from that storage's `AH_META_WORKSPACELESS_DB_KEY`. The added tests construct the realistic host-owned workspaceless state separately and prove that create/resume system messages must be byte-identical. `CopilotSessionLauncher` maps the flag into `IAgentHostPromptContext`, and `AgentHostPromptRegistry` conditionally appends `AGENT_HOST_WORKSPACELESS_INSTRUCTIONS`; therefore losing the flag changed the provider-bound system prompt on resume. Repository configuration explicitly documents that stable system prompts enable cross-session prompt-cache reuse, and SDK usage metadata exposes prompt-cache writes. The blamed base line is the old provider-storage-only lookup introduced by be2aeccba1a5853e07d22d23f0419a6e2a4b4cee.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore the default chat of a workspaceless conversation after release or Agent Host restart, then send the first new turn
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first send waits for host/session metadata restoration, SDK client acquisition, customization snapshot construction, one SDK resume, and then the provider model request. The changed host-map lookup is synchronous and negligible; its performance significance is that the provider-bound system prompt now matches creation before the first model request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/read the session metadata database or session-state metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata read for the default resume; no additional read is introduced by the map lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same metadata read occurred, but `workspaceless` was taken only from the opened provider storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to resolve working-directory and launch metadata before resume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per coalesced cold resume, overlapped with host metadata loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must settle before the launch plan is built.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resume the Copilot SDK session with the resolved system message
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful call per coalesced restore, apart from pre-existing bounded error fallbacks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same resume call, but workspaceless restores could send a different system prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks session availability and the triggering turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit the first resumed model request whose prefix includes the resolved system message
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider request per user turn; the first post-resume request determines whether the prior prompt prefix can be reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The request already occurred, but a changed workspaceless prompt forced uncached prefix processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly controls prompt-prefill work and time to first output.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One restore per cold/resident-miss session; concurrent restore attempts for the same SDK session are coalesced by `CopilotSessionLifetime.resumeDefault`, so effective cardinality is one resume and one launch prompt per session restore, not one per caller.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Metadata loading and `client.getSessionMetadata` are overlapped in `_resumeSessionOnce`; same-session resumes are coalesced to one promise. Distinct sessions may restore concurrently under existing client/session controls; the diff does not increase that concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the diff, a host-owned `workspaceless=true` could be absent from the SDK-session database, causing resume to omit the scratch block and miss the conversation's exact prompt cache. The new host-first value keeps the launch prompt stable; provider metadata remains a fallback when host settings are unavailable. Cold-cache work is otherwise unchanged, while a valid warm prompt can now be reused.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed flag directly controls conditional prompt content, tests prove create/resume message identity, and repository configuration documents prompt stability as the condition for cache reuse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency savings depend on model, provider cache lifetime, prompt length, and whether a usable cache entry still exists.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. This is a concrete cache-lifecycle fix; it was recorded with `report_regression_fix` and introduces no new boundary or multiplicity.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore an addressed peer or fork chat in a workspaceless owning session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A send to a nonresident addressed chat waits for its metadata read, working-directory resolution, customization snapshot, and one SDK resume before the turn proceeds. The new launch-plan field only changes prompt selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read addressed-chat metadata, and lazily read owner metadata only if working-directory data requires it
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One addressed-chat read per restore, with at most one owner read through the memoized `readOwnerMetadata` closure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same read count; the addressed resume did not forward the resulting workspaceless value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Supplies the launch working directory and prompt flag before SDK resume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per coalesced addressed-chat restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same call count with a prompt missing workspaceless guidance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the first turn to that chat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the first provider model request after addressed-chat resume
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per user turn, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same request, but the resumed prompt could differ from the chat's original prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A stable prompt can reuse cache; an unstable one requires prompt processing before output.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per distinct addressed chat restored. Duplicate concurrent restores of the same chat are coalesced by `resumePeer(chatKey)`; different chat keys can proceed independently under existing lifetime leases.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-chat resume coalescing prevents duplicate same-key SDK calls. The diff neither adds a loop nor changes aggregate concurrency across distinct chats.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The owning session's retained setting now supplies `workspaceless` even when the addressed chat database lacks the marker, preserving the prompt used when the backing was minted. Metadata files and customization snapshots retain their prior cold/warm behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the launch plan now forwards the already-read flag and the prompt registry deterministically appends the workspaceless block only when true.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of users with multiple addressed chats and provider cache-hit duration is not measured here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added work is a constant map/property read; boundary counts and concurrency are unchanged, while prompt-cache reuse improves.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mint a new peer chat or fork from a workspaceless session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat creation waits for existing customization/snapshot work. A fresh peer performs one SDK create; a fork first resolves its source, performs one SDK fork RPC and one database copy, then performs one SDK resume. The added setting lookup and launch-plan property do not create or move any boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fork the source SDK session at a turn boundary
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one RPC per explicit fork; zero for a non-fork peer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks fork creation before the forked session can resume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy the source SQLite session database with `VACUUM INTO`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One database copy per explicit fork, scaling with source database size; zero for a fresh peer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a fresh peer SDK session or resume the newly forked SDK session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create for a peer or one resume for a fork, per minted chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same one launch call, but without the parent's workspaceless prompt layer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the first model request in the minted chat with its system prompt
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per user turn, unchanged; effective prompt-cache reuse depends on shared stable prefix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same request count; omission of the parent flag made the prompt inconsistent and could prevent reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Prompt prefill is on the response critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the number of explicitly created peers/forks, one launch per chat. There is no changed collection fan-out. Fork database-copy cost continues to scale with source history size, but that mechanism is pre-existing and unaffected.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Minting uses the existing session/source queue, serializing operations that share the source unless `independentQueue` is explicitly requested. The diff does not change queue selection or launch concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A new peer/fork now receives the same workspaceless prompt layer as its parent. On a cold provider cache this adds only the required bounded instruction block; when compatible prompt prefixes are cached, stability permits reuse rather than defeating it. No host metadata cache is invalidated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged boundary cardinality and queueing: the changed lines only read a retained `ResourceMap` value and thread it into existing plans.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact cache sharing across separate SDK chat IDs and model families is provider-dependent, but no adverse scaling mechanism is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded prompt addition preserves intended semantics and stability; existing fork RPC/database-copy costs are not materially amplified.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all changed files and hunks. No diff-introduced actionable performance issue was found. The change fixes a host/provider metadata mismatch that destabilized workspaceless system prompts and defeated warm prompt-cache reuse; the introducing commit was identified and the regression fix was recorded.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
